# proverb.py — Implementation Guide

## Contract (from README + public_test.py)

`proverb(*items, qualifier=None) -> list[str]`

- Variadic positional nouns (`*items`). Callers splat a list: `proverb(*input_data, qualifier=None)`.
- Keyword-only `qualifier` (it follows `*items`). Public test always passes `qualifier=None`; other callers may pass a string.
- Return a **list of lines**, not a joined string. Empty input → `[]`.
- Every line is input-dependent. Do not hardcode any full sentence (including the closer). The README example is illustrative, not a template of fixed text.

Example (README):

```
["nail", "shoe", "horse", "rider", "message", "battle", "kingdom"]
```

yields six pair lines plus a closer that names the first item:

```
For want of a nail the shoe was lost.
For want of a shoe the horse was lost.
...
For want of a battle the kingdom was lost.
And all for the want of a nail.
```

## Signature

Replace the empty stub with:

```python
def proverb(*items, qualifier=None):
```

Do not accept a single list argument. Tests unpack. `qualifier` must be keyword-only so `proverb("nail", "shoe")` stays valid.

## Data

No extra types. `items` is a tuple of strings. Build one Python list of line strings and return it.

Line shapes (the only two formats):

| Role | Format |
|---|---|
| Pair `i → i+1` | `For want of a {items[i]} the {items[i+1]} was lost.` |
| Closer | `And all for the want of a {subject}.` |

`subject` is `items[0]` when `qualifier` is `None`/absent; otherwise `"{qualifier} {items[0]}"` (one space). Example: `qualifier="horseshoe"` and first item `"nail"` → `And all for the want of a horseshoe nail.`

Articles stay `"a"`; no a/an logic. Items are interpolated as given.

## Algorithm

1. If `len(items) == 0`, return `[]`. Do not emit a closer (there is no first item).
2. `lines = []`.
3. For `i` in `range(len(items) - 1)`: append the pair line for `(items[i], items[i+1])`. One item ⇒ this loop is a no-op.
4. Build `subject`:
   - `qualifier` is `None` or otherwise empty/falsy → `subject = items[0]`.
   - otherwise → `subject = f"{qualifier} {items[0]}"`.
5. Append `f"And all for the want of a {subject}."`.
6. Return `lines`.

O(n) time, O(n) extra strings. No recursion, no regex, no join-then-split.

## Edge cases

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `proverb()` / `proverb(*[])` | `[]` — public test |
| One item, `qualifier=None` | Only the closer: `["And all for the want of a {item}."]`. Zero pair lines. |
| Two items | One pair line + closer naming the **first** item. |
| Three+ items | `n-1` consecutive pair lines + closer on `items[0]`. Adjacent pairs only; never skip or wrap. |
| Arbitrary nouns / length | Same templates. Content is not restricted to the horseshoe rhyme. |
| `qualifier` omitted or `None` | Closer uses bare `items[0]`. |
| `qualifier` non-empty string | Closer prefixes that word, then a space, then `items[0]`. Pair lines never mention the qualifier. |
| Empty-string qualifier | Treat as absent (falsy): do not insert a double space (`"a  nail"`). |

Punctuation is exact: period at end of every line, no trailing spaces, no trailing newline on a line, no blank lines.

- Do not hardcode `"And all for the want of a nail."` or any other full line.
- Do not put `qualifier` into pair lines.
- Do not use the last item in the closer; always the first.
- Do not mutate caller input; `*items` is already a tuple.
- No classes, helpers, or constants for full sentences. Tiny local format strings (or f-strings) are enough.

# proverb.py — Implementation Guide

## Contract (from README + public_test.py)

`proverb(*items, qualifier=None) -> list[str]`

- Variadic positional nouns (`*items`). Callers splat a list: `proverb(*input_data, qualifier=None)`.
- Keyword-only `qualifier` (it follows `*items`). Public test always passes `qualifier=None`; other callers may pass a string.
- Return a **list of lines**, not a joined string. Empty input → `[]`.
- Every line is input-dependent. Do not hardcode any full sentence (including the closer). The README example is illustrative, not a template of fixed text.

Example (README):

```
["nail", "shoe", "horse", "rider", "message", "battle", "kingdom"]
```

yields six pair lines plus a closer that names the first item:

```
For want of a nail the shoe was lost.
For want of a shoe the horse was lost.
...
For want of a battle the kingdom was lost.
And all for the want of a nail.
```

## Signature

Replace the empty stub with:

```python
def proverb(*items, qualifier=None):
```

Do not accept a single list argument. Tests unpack. `qualifier` must be keyword-only so `proverb("nail", "shoe")` stays valid.

## Data

No extra types. `items` is a tuple of strings. Build one Python list of line strings and return it.

Line shapes (the only two formats):

| Role | Format |
|---|---|
| Pair `i → i+1` | `For want of a {items[i]} the {items[i+1]} was lost.` |
| Closer | `And all for the want of a {subject}.` |

`subject` is `items[0]` when `qualifier` is `None`/absent; otherwise `"{qualifier} {items[0]}"` (one space). Example: `qualifier="horseshoe"` and first item `"nail"` → `And all for the want of a horseshoe nail.`

Articles stay `"a"`; no a/an logic. Items are interpolated as given.

## Algorithm

1. If `len(items) == 0`, return `[]`. Do not emit a closer (there is no first item).
2. `lines = []`.
3. For `i` in `range(len(items) - 1)`: append the pair line for `(items[i], items[i+1])`. One item ⇒ this loop is a no-op.
4. Build `subject`:
   - `qualifier` is `None` or otherwise empty/falsy → `subject = items[0]`.
   - otherwise → `subject = f"{qualifier} {items[0]}"`.
5. Append `f"And all for the want of a {subject}."`.
6. Return `lines`.

O(n) time, O(n) extra strings. No recursion, no regex, no join-then-split.

## Edge cases

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `proverb()` / `proverb(*[])` | `[]` — public test |
| One item, `qualifier=None` | Only the closer: `["And all for the want of a {item}."]`. Zero pair lines. |
| Two items | One pair line + closer naming the **first** item. |
| Three+ items | `n-1` consecutive pair lines + closer on `items[0]`. Adjacent pairs only; never skip or wrap. |
| Arbitrary nouns / length | Same templates. Content is not restricted to the horseshoe rhyme. |
| `qualifier` omitted or `None` | Closer uses bare `items[0]`. |
| `qualifier` non-empty string | Closer prefixes that word, then a space, then `items[0]`. Pair lines never mention the qualifier. |
| Empty-string qualifier | Treat as absent (falsy): do not insert a double space (`"a  nail"`). |

Punctuation is exact: period at end of every line, no trailing spaces, no trailing newline on a line, no blank lines.

## What not to do

- Do not `return "\n".join(lines)` or a single string. Tests `assertEqual` against a list.
- Do not hardcode `"And all for the want of a nail."` or any other full line.
- Do not put `qualifier` into pair lines.
- Do not use the last item in the closer; always the first.
- Do not mutate caller input; `*items` is already a tuple.
- No classes, helpers, or constants for full sentences. Tiny local format strings (or f-strings) are enough.
